text.title: Retainer Pricing Methodology — Output Contract
text.summary: JSON Schema (draft-07) for the retainer spec: exactly one named shape with its defining terms (block-of-hours with rollover and overage, outcome-based with a deliverable list, availability with response time and maximum load, or a hybrid that says which shape invoices and which clause settles scope), a price shown as expected hours x hourly rate x multiple with the multiple at or above 1.3 or a named concession, written inclusions, exclusions and a turnaround, a minimum term of 3 months, 30 days notice and a price review within 12 months, invoicing in advance, a phase-out plan with the 3-month hourly average and a cutover date when converting an hourly client, a capacity ledger that stays within available hours, and a 6-month outcome review with the hours ledger and the action it forces. Validator at scripts/validate-retainer-pricing-methodology.py enforces it, including the price arithmetic, the phase-out floor, the capacity sum and the review rules.

required.field: first day of the first retainer period

`kind` block_of_hours, outcome_based, availability or hybrid, with `block_of_hours` (`prepaid_hours_per_month`, `rollover` none / one_period / capped with `rollover_cap_hours`, `overage_hourly_rate`), `outcome_based` (`deliverables_per_period[]`), `availability` (`response_time_business_hours`, `max_monthly_load_hours`) or `hybrid` (`invoicing_shape`, `scope_dispute_clause`) as the kind requires (r-retainer-shape-named, r-scope-inclusions-exclusions-and-turnaround)

`expected_monthly_hours` (maximum load for availability), `hourly_rate`, `currency`, `monthly_price`, `multiple` = monthly_price / (hours x rate) at or above 1.3, or `concession` twelve_month_minimum_term / full_term_prepaid when below (r-rate-floor-1-3x-hourly-equivalent)
`minimum_months` at least 3, `notice_days` at least 30, `price_review_date` at most 12 months after `start_date` (r-term-notice-and-price-review)

null for a new client; otherwise `avg_billed_hours_last_3_months`, `avg_monthly_spend_last_3_months`, `cutover_date`, `parallel_billing_periods` at most 1; the price is at or above 1.3 x the average spend (r-hourly-phase-out-plan)

`available_billable_hours_per_month`, `committed_hours_other_retainers`, `committed_hours_this_retainer` (= expected monthly hours), `total_after_signing` = their sum, at or below available (r-capacity-not-oversold)

`scheduled_date` 6 months after `start_date`; `findings` null until held, then `still_active_without_renegotiation`, `periods[]` with `paid_hours` and `actual_hours`, `effective_hourly_rate`, `action` none / re_scope / rate_increase / address_usage as the two-period rules require (r-six-month-outcome-review)

forbidden.pattern: `shape.kind` without the matching terms object, or a hybrid without `invoicing_shape` and `scope_dispute_clause` — fm-01-hourly-with-a-deposit
`pricing.multiple` below 1.3 with `concession` null, or a `multiple` that is not monthly_price / (expected_monthly_hours x hourly_rate) — fm-02-below-floor-for-predictability
`rollover` capped with no `rollover_cap_hours`, or any rollover value that lets hours accumulate indefinitely — fm-03-unbounded-rollover
`term.minimum_months` below 3, `notice_days` below 30, or `price_review_date` more than 12 months after the start — fm-04-cancel-any-time-retainer

`hourly_phase_out.parallel_billing_periods` above 1, a `cutover_date` before `start_date`, or a `monthly_price` below 1.3 x `avg_monthly_spend_last_3_months` without a concession — fm-05-parallel-hourly-and-retainer
`capacity.total_after_signing` above `available_billable_hours_per_month`, or not equal to other plus this retainer — fm-06-capacity-sold-twice

`outcome_review.scheduled_date` not 6 months after the start, or findings where actual hours exceed paid hours in two consecutive periods with `action` none, or below 50 percent of paid in two consecutive periods without `action` address_usage (r-six-month-outcome-review)

example.note: One shape with rollover limited to one period and an overage rate; 6,240 EUR = 40 h x 120 EUR x 1.3, and 1.3 x the client's 4,560 EUR three-month average is 5,928, so the price clears both floors without a concession; 60 + 40 = 100 of 120 available hours; the price review falls 11 months after the start and the outcome review 6 months after.

An availability retainer with no response time or maximum load; priced at 0.95x the hourly equivalent with no concession; no written exclusions and a turnaround of zero in a unit that is not business hours or days; one month minimum, no notice, a price review three years out; billed in arrears on net 60; a cutover before the start and three parallel periods; committed hours reported as 120 when 100 + 40 is 140 and exceeds capacity; the outcome review scheduled 15 months out.

list.item: `shape.kind` is one of the four and its terms object is present; a hybrid says which shape invoices and which clause settles scope; block-of-hours rollover is none, one period or capped.
`pricing.multiple` = `monthly_price` / (`expected_monthly_hours` x `hourly_rate`), at or above 1.3 or with a named concession; for availability the expected hours equal `max_monthly_load_hours`.
Inclusions, exclusions and a turnaround in business hours or days are written; the meeting count is stated.
Minimum term at least 3 months, notice at least 30 days, price review within 12 months of `start_date`; invoiced in advance with payment due before the period starts.
Converting an hourly client: the 3-month average is shown, `monthly_price` is at or above 1.3 x the average spend, `cutover_date` is on or after `start_date`, at most one parallel period.

`capacity.total_after_signing` = other + this retainer and is within available hours; `outcome_review.scheduled_date` is 6 months after the start, and findings force re-scope or rate increase after two overrun periods and address usage after two periods below 50 percent.

text.reference: Validator implementing this schema and the cross-field rules (price multiple arithmetic, availability hours equal to maximum load, phase-out floor and cutover, capacity sum and ceiling, price review within 12 months, review at 6 months and the two-period actions).
The same schema as a standalone file.
